name: table-count
description: Number of Drizzle pgTable() definitions across shared/. The mature-machine north star is a SMALLER schema (<=450 tables); today's count is far above it. This strict down-only ratchet makes the schema monotonic: adding a table fails CI until the baseline is deliberately bumped (a conscious 'yes we need this'), and every consolidation lowers the baseline toward the target. Founder-chosen 'strict' 2026-07-16.
lastBumpNote: 759 -> 760 on 2026-08-12: scenarios -- the economics layer's versioned deterministic hypothesis (BI12, BK24, canonical law 4). Earned because decision_snapshots froze what was KNOWN (evidence) and what was ASSUMED (assumptions) but had nowhere to point for the ECONOMICS that justified the choice: a snapshot could record 'offer $42,000' while the arithmetic behind the number lived nowhere at all, so a year later you could reconstruct what the investor believed about the PARCEL and not what they believed about the DEAL. One row per computed hypothesis carrying the engine that produced it, that engine's VERSION (NOT NULL -- an unversioned number cannot be defended once the formula moves), the VERBATIM inputs the engine consumed, and the outputs. This does not invent a mechanism: note_payoff_quotes already persists engine_version + day_count_convention + engine_input_json as 'the verbatim input snapshot so the number can be recomputed and defended years later' (server/services/notePaymentMath.ts) -- BK23's contract, already exemplary in ONE vertical, now generalised. IMMUTABLE: no updated_at column and no UPDATE path; re-running the maths INSERTs a new scenario, because a mutable one would let improving a formula silently rewrite the meaning of every number the old formula produced -- the economics equivalent of the mutable-decision failure law 6 forbids. The engine registry is CLOSED with no escape hatch for 'call a model and store the answer' (BL3's fail condition for deterministic money math is literally 'a model response is required to reproduce a financial result'), and a test asserts scenario.ts contains no model/fetch/dynamic-import reference at all -- the guarantee is an absent branch, not a policy. A null metric means UNDEFINED, never zero: an IRR has no solution for some cash-flow shapes and rendering that as 0% is a different, false claim. NOT REUSING scenario_simulations / scenario_outcome_comparisons: those are FOUNDER-plane autopilot LLM war-gaming tables, and reusing one would make Founder OS the owner of customer financial truth, which BI5 forbids. No FK on subject_id because the economics of a deal you walked away from are exactly the ones worth still being able to read.
